title: Tell a deoptimisation from a tier change in a compile log

cases.says: a method compiled at tier 3 and then tier 4 runs at tier 4, a getter at tier 1, and a method with no compile line runs in the interpreter
tier-4 code made not entrant with no newer compile of the method counts as one deoptimisation
an OSR compile of the method's loop is not the code a new call enters
a tier-3 compile made not entrant after a tier-4 compile was installed leaves calls in the tier-4 code, not in the interpreter
after the tier-4 code is thrown away and the method is compiled again at tier 3, calls run at tier 3, not at the highest tier the method ever reached
a lower tier's code made not entrant because a newer compile replaced it is not a deoptimisation
code made not entrant before any newer compile existed is a deoptimisation, even if a higher tier is compiled later

origin.section: Compiled Code Rests on Assumptions, and a Class Loaded Later Can Make It Not Entrant
